newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela overnight lending rate rockets to 90 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela overnight lending rate rockets to 90 pct.

text.p: Venezuela's overnight interbank lending rate shot up to a maximum level of 90 percent Monday, from about 20 percent Friday, as normally liquid money markets dried up, traders said.
Traders said the sudden shortage of funds was caused by a combination of factors, including heavy dollar buying and a large auction of Central Bank Monetary Stabilization, or TEM, bills last week.
"The money is concentrated in a few banks. The overnight rose today basically because banks were paying for dollar purchases from the Central Bank last Thursday," one trader said.
"The market dried up and that led to rates of up to 90 percent," another trader said.
Traders said the rate would gradually return to more moderate levels by the end of the week.
"We won't see it at five percent but at about 40 percent by the end of the week," one said.
